title: The Dramatic change in the weather
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：dramatic　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dramatic 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the tailor wrote of ① a dramatic change in the weather in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② more dramatic than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the dramatic ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most dramatic change in the weather anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the order for November 1943 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dramatic to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the dramatic ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dramatic turn in the match, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dramatic as the turn in the match they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dramatic or not, and he said so.

By 1956 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dramatic, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite dramatic; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the dramatic ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1959, year after year, she wrote of another dramatic change in the weather in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more dramatic than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most dramatic turn in the match in the whole shop, she said in 1961, was the one she could never quite name; the dramatic ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 戏剧性（前置定语 a dramatic change in the weather：1949 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件戏剧性的突变）
B. adj. 戏剧性／引人注目（比较级 more dramatic than：文中两处，一处比天气的突变，一处比预想）
C. adj. 戏剧性／引人注目（最高级 the most dramatic：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 戏剧性（表语 too dramatic to do：母亲觉得它太戏剧性，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 引人注目（前置定语 a dramatic turn in the match：叔叔把整件事称作一桩引人注目的转折）
F. adj. 引人注目（同级比较 as dramatic as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩比赛的转折相比）
G. adj. 引人注目（后置定语 something dramatic：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 引人注目（受程度副词修饰 quite dramatic：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a dramatic change in the weather
the most dramatic change in the weather anybody
a dramatic turn in the match
The most dramatic turn in the match in

answers.why: dramatic 意为“戏剧性”，1949 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件戏剧性的突变”，此处作前置定语 a dramatic change in the weather。
dramatic 意为“戏剧性”，此处用比较级 more dramatic than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
dramatic 意为“戏剧性”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说它是裁缝铺里最戏剧性的一件，故用最高级 the most dramatic change in the weather。
dramatic 意为“戏剧性”，母亲认为这件东西“太戏剧性了，谁也用不上”，too dramatic to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩引人注目的转折”，此处作前置定语 a dramatic turn in the match。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩比赛的转折一样引人注目”，同级比较用 as dramatic as。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“引人注目的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dramatic。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当引人注目”，quite 修饰原级 dramatic。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，1959 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要引人注目”，故用比较级 more dramatic than。
dramatic 意为“引人注目”，母亲 1961 年说的是“整个裁缝铺里最引人注目的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most dramatic turn in the match。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件戏剧性的突变。（a dramatic change in the weather）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更戏剧性。（more dramatic than …）
母亲觉得它太戏剧性，谁也用不上。（too dramatic to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩引人注目的转折。（a dramatic turn in the match）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩比赛的转折一样引人注目。（as dramatic as …）
到了 1956 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件引人注目的东西。（something dramatic）
answers: In 1949 the tailor wrote of a dramatic change in the weather in the order.
Everybody said it was more dramatic than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too dramatic to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dramatic turn in the match.
He said nobody would call it as dramatic as the turn in the match they had once had.
By 1956 the order asked for nothing but something dramatic.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dramatic 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the tailor wrote of a dramatic change in the weather in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most dramatic change in the weather in the shop, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too dramatic to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dramatic turn in the match, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite dramatic, and everybody laughed.
The dramatic ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
